summary.oneLiner: Listed 2026-05-25 · band Rs.52 to Rs.55 · offer document not yet processed

one-line thesis: A ₹51cr-revenue NSE-SME cashew processor that has just completed its first full year in a larger plant and
its IPO: FY26 revenue +43% to ₹51cr, PAT +68% to ₹4.53cr, driven almost entirely by better utilisation of the
6,000 MT Ghiloth facility it moved into in June (FY26) plus the acquisition of Yashvardhan Food Industries,
which internalised labour. The business is still ~95% cashew and ~94–95% B2B, so the whole FY27 story is
three deliberate diversifications management put a number on — manufacturing to ₹60–65cr, mix to 70:30
cashew:others, and B2B down to 90–93% with B2G (NAFED / GeM / canteen tenders) as the stated priority — plus
one hard-dated new vertical, a CNSL extraction unit with machinery already ordered and commercial production
guided for August–September 2026. Management explicitly declined to guide mid-term margins.
financial scorecard (track qoq/yoy): Management reported FY26 full-year figures only; no discrete H2 P&L was given on the call.
> Adjustments / one-offs: management flagged no one-off or accounting distortion. Two structural
> distortions to carry forward, both in management's words: (a) FY26 is not like-for-like on capacity —
> "we just shifted from a smaller capacity to this bigger unit last year in June", so the base year ran a
> smaller plant; (b) FY26 includes the acquisition of Yashvardhan Food Industries Private Limited, which
> "significantly strengthened our manufacturing capabilities and also reduced our dependency on the labor
> cost" — the revenue/EBITDA step-up is therefore part organic-utilisation, part acquired. Management did
guidance (critical — verify next quarter: Revenue / manufacturing scale (FY27): "this year we are targeting approximately INR60 crores to INR65
crores of manufacturing itself" (vs cashew manufacturing "approximately INR35 crores in that INR51 crores"
in FY26). Note this is the manufacturing line, not consolidated revenue — management did not guide a
consolidated FY27 revenue number.
Margin: "the EBITDA levels between 16% to 20% is sustainable throughout, but uncertainty always lies
there because there are cross-border imports which are involved". Mid-term margin aspiration explicitly
refused: "I'm not allowed to specify anything regarding the numbers of future-looking statements, so I
won't be able to answer that."
Volume / utilisation (FY27): "last year … we achieved approximately 3,200 MT and this year we are
targeting approximately 4,000 to 4,200 MT out of 6,000" → "around 65% to 70%".
Utilisation (2-year): "our target is to reach at least 85% to 90% of capacity utilization in next two
years" — conditioned on "additional working capital and increasing demand and … penetrating the
institutional supplies".
Product mix (medium-term): "We are targeting that we should make it ideally 70-30 split … 70 being
cashew" (from ~95% cashew today).
Channel mix (FY27): from "94%, 95% to 2.5% only" → "we'll try to make it around 90% to 93% in B2B and
have an increase in B2G followed up by B2C. Our target is more towards B2G this year."
Capex / commissioning date: CNSL unit — "We have already ordered the required machinery and we are
expecting the commercial production from August to September in 2026." ← the one hard date on this call.
order book & pipeline: No order book (spot/commodity FMCG model). The pipeline management described is channel access rather than
contracted volume:
B2G (the stated FY27 priority): "we are supplying to NAFED, now we are penetrating ourselves into
other government places and PSUs which uses gift hampers for supplying. There's GeM portal in it."
Addressable set named: "there are central CRPF canteens, then police canteens, then we have army supplies
generally, then we have the BSF supplies … there are railway supplies as well and other than that there
are tenders on GeM portal from IOC, BHEL and other PSUs for the gift hampers in which they take up as 500
grams packaging, consumer packaging."
B2B: "all the segments which are institutional demands, wholesale suppliers, all the HoReCa supplies,
restaurants, sweets".
Geography: presence "across 17 states" in FY26; near-term plan is depth not breadth — "our first target
is to penetrate deeper and deeper within next 2 years in Northern and Western zone".
No value, tenure or conversion timeline was attached to any of the above.
segment / subsidiary detail: Cashew (core, ~95%): "It's mostly cashew, around 95% is cashew only because we are the third largest
North Indian processor as well." Manufacturing split: cashew "approximately INR35 crores in that INR51
crores" (FY26) vs "approximately INR22 crores" (FY25).
Processing volumes: FY25 "approximately 1,800 MT to 1,900 MT"; FY26 "approximately 3,000 to 3,200 MT of
capacity utilization, including everything". Growth attributed squarely to the plant move: "the growth is
purely because of the better utilization of the capacity during the last fiscal year. In FY26, we shifted
in June from our earlier smaller unit."
Traded nuts / other dry fruits: "we are also into raw cashew nuts trading and trading of other nuts
such as makhana, almonds, walnuts" — plus "raisins, trail mixes and we are now also entering in various
other segments such as some kinds of seeds, munakkas and spices."
SKUs: "there will be approximately 12 to 13 SKUs in our portfolios, but more or less the major
consumption lies between cashews, almonds, walnuts and pistachios."
Channels: B2B / B2C / B2G, currently "94%, 95% to 2.5% only".
Sourcing network: "sourcing network from Africa for cashews, makhana from Bihar and also from other
importers and processors of almonds, walnuts, raisins"; raisins "are directly procured from the
Maharashtrian region, Sangli".
Subsidiary: Yashvardhan Food Industries Private Limited, acquired in FY26 — rationale given was
manufacturing capability + labour-cost dependency + capacity utilisation. No standalone financials given.
People: ~140 employees; "around seven to eight people" in sales, including "director sales" and a
"national head sales who comes in with the experience around 15 years"; "four to five people deployed in
the Khari Baoli and all the Delhi NCR region"; "two people at the back end".
growth verticals / optionality: CNSL (cashew nut shell liquid) — the genuinely new vertical. "currently the cashew shell generated
during processing is sold as a by-product. Going forward, we are setting up a facility to extract CNSL,
which has a higher demand in industrial use as oil in paints, coatings and other industrial applications.
After extracting the oil, the remaining calorific biomass will be supplied to energy furnaces and it can
be used as a material for burning in high-speed boilers." Machinery ordered; commercial production guided
August–September 2026. No revenue, capex or margin number was attached to it on the call.
B2G institutional supply — NAFED today, GeM/PSU gift-hamper tenders + defence/paramilitary/railway
canteens targeted (see §4). Management called this the priority: "Our target is more towards B2G this year."
B2C, deliberately capital-light. "if you purely see that commodity business, generally the B2C segment
the gross margins are somewhere around – the gross margin is around 30% to 25% and the COGS around 70%. So
due to which the margins for marketing or the cash burning which is required in B2C is very less. Right
now we are organically profitable and we want to expand slowly into B2C segment only."
Spices as the geographic key. Management framed spices, not nuts, as the route out of the North/West:
"Our target for other parts will be when we'll be entering the other products such as spices in future,
which we are planning and we are in the R&D stage of that."
Latent capacity — 6,000 MT installed against 3,200 MT done; the 85–90% two-year utilisation target is
the single largest identified growth lever, gated on working capital.
6a. moat & competitive position: Physical position in Asia's largest dry-fruit mandi. "we have a dedicated outlet at Khari Baoli, Delhi,
which is Asia's largest wholesale spice and dry fruit market, which helps us enable a direct connection
with the customers, have a better market intelligence and efficient distribution." Four-to-five of ~140
employees are deployed there — a small, durable distribution/price-discovery node rather than a claim.
Scale claim in its own region: "we are the third largest North Indian processor as well" (management
assertion; not independently evidenced on the call).
Origin sourcing network, cited as the reason to stay cashew-led: "our core strength is cashews, our
network in Africa, we have given time and the margins are good, we have all the infrastructure, we have
been known for cashew leaders."
Backward integration into manufacturing (vs pure trading) is the stated margin defence: asked whether
18% EBITDA was sustainable in a commodity business, the answer was "we have integrated it with the
manufacturing and the EBITDA levels between 16% to 20% is sustainable" — and the traded-only lines
corroborate the gap (almonds 4–5% vs the manufactured cashew business).
Demand-side geography match: cashew consumption sits where the company sits — "the major consumption
lies between North and Western region because they are used heavily in sweets, in gravies", while "the
processing lies mostly towards the Southern part or the Eastern part of the country."
margins & cost dynamics: Company-level EBITDA: FY26 EBITDA ₹9.24cr, "nearly doubled". The transcript's FY26 margin % is garbled
(§2) and management never restated it. The only margin levels spoken on the call are the analyst's
premise ("the EBITDA margins are at a higher level which are before the IPO, which is 18%") and
management's own sustainable band, "16% to 20%".
Product-level margins (management, verbatim): raisins "10% to 12%"; almonds — "the most voluminous
product and the margins lies between 4% to 5%"; walnuts "8% to 10%"; pistachios "11% to 12%".
→ Diversifying away from cashew is margin-dilutive at the product line, which management conceded
directly: "in other products, the margin is slightly lesser because we are into trading part of that and
this is, there's no certain kind of manufacturing which can be done in other products."
B2C economics: "the gross margin is around 30% to 25% and the COGS around 70%."
The stated margin lever is fixed-cost absorption, not price: "we have been targeting to increase the
volume in processing, which will help us to have a better utilization of the capacity, which will reduce
the fixed cost of the plant and other indirect expenses, which can help us improve the EBITDA margins."
Labour: the Yashvardhan Food Industries acquisition "reduced our dependency on the labor cost".
Freight / logistics (see §10 and §13): volatility acknowledged but FY26 impact denied on timing grounds
— "because our raw material dispatches have started since May only, so we have not been affected that
much … the shipments have started now and the prices have come down again, so there's not a major impact
in the freight costs."
Named margin risks: "there are cross-border imports which are involved and, you know, there are some
uncertain situations such as increase in the local freight cost of containers or prices hike in
transportations."
capex / expansion (watch slippage): CNSL extraction facility — the only dated capex item. "We have already ordered the required machinery
and we are expecting the commercial production from August to September in 2026." Capex amount not
disclosed; expected revenue/margin not disclosed. Slippage watch: machinery-ordered → commercial
production inside ~2 months of the call is a tight window for a first-time process line.
Processing plant: already-executed capex — the FY26 move "in June from our earlier smaller unit" to the
6,000 MT facility. No new processing-capacity capex was announced; the plan is to fill the existing
6,000 MT ("we are targeting in next two years with additional working capital … to reach at least 85% to
90% of capacity utilization"), i.e. the next two years' growth is guided to be working-capital-funded,
not capex-funded.
Spices remain pre-capex: "we are in the R&D stage of that."
capital allocation: IPO proceeds, in management's words: "The object of the issue was used in part of it was used in the
debt repayment, part of it was used in the working capital which will be -- which is used in increasing
the capacity utilization and part of it was GCP and issue expenses."
Debt repayment quantum: "we are repaying around INR9.5 crores of debt towards from the issue proceeds."
Management could not confirm the resulting leverage on the call — "that I have to exactly check how much".
Stated rationale: "when we are repaying the debt, it will directly benefit our EBITDA levels, the PAT
margin levels in further and future and the working capital will benefit us in having a better reach
towards the capacity utilization and also penetrating into other verticals of dry fruit trading."
M&A: one acquisition executed in FY26 (Yashvardhan Food Industries Private Limited); consideration not
disclosed on the call.
No dividend, buyback or further fund-raise was discussed.
risks & watch-items: Single-product concentration: ~95% cashew today; the 70:30 target is medium-term and the diversifying
products carry lower margins (§7).
Single-channel concentration: B2B at "94%, 95%"; B2G is the stated fix but is tender-driven and
currently near-nil.
Commodity + import exposure, acknowledged by management as the reason the margin band can break:
"because it is a commodity business, there is slight fluctuation … there are cross-border imports which
are involved."
Freight/container cost: acknowledged as an industry-wide problem in the prior 2–3 months ("all
industries are facing some trans-logistic problems … Yes, it is there"), escaped in FY26 only by
procurement seasonality — "the procurement period for cashew nuts or any other products is generally from
January to May". A repeat of the freight spike inside the Jan–May FY28 procurement window would land
squarely on cost.
Working capital is the binding constraint on the utilisation ramp — the 85–90% target is explicitly
conditioned on "additional working capital", against a business that has just used IPO money to deleverage.
Leverage: analyst-cited D/E of 1.73 for FY26 against ₹9.5cr of repayment; management did not confirm
the post-repayment number.
CNSL execution risk: first-time process, no capex/return disclosed, tight Aug–Sep 2026 window.
Disclosure quality: no H2-discrete P&L, no consolidated FY27 revenue guidance, no capex quantum, and a
garbled EBITDA-margin statement that went uncorrected on the call.
Governance/liquidity structure: NSE SME (Series SM), micro-cap, first year of listed disclosure.
management quality / tone: Measured and unusually concrete for an SME first-year call: the MD volunteered volumes (MT), per-product
margin bands and channel percentages without being pushed, and answered the awkward "is 18% sustainable in a
commodity business?" question head-on with a band and its failure conditions rather than a deflection. Two
tone markers worth carrying forward. First, he declined to give a mid-term margin aspiration on
compliance grounds — "I'm not allowed to specify anything regarding the numbers of future-looking statements"
— restraint, though it sat oddly beside the FY27 manufacturing, volume and mix targets he had already given.
Second, he could not answer the post-repayment leverage question ("that I have to exactly check how
much") and allowed the analyst to supply the debt figures; the CFO (Mr. Anil Kumar Gupta) was on the call but
did not speak at any point in the transcript. Diversification was framed honestly as margin-dilutive rather
than sold as accretive. Only five questions were asked, by two analysts, and the call ran ~8 transcript
pages — coverage is thin and the disclosures are unaudited-by-questioning.
non-obvious takeaways: The 43% growth is a plant-move artefact more than a demand event. Management said so plainly: "the
growth is purely because of the better utilization of the capacity during the last fiscal year." FY25 ran
1,800–1,900 MT in a smaller unit; FY26 ran 3,000–3,200 MT in the new one. The comparable FY27 delta
(3,200 → 4,000–4,200 MT) is ~25–31% on volume, a materially slower step — the 43% is not the run-rate.
Diversification and margin pull in opposite directions. Every product being added (almonds 4–5%,
raisins 10–12%, walnuts 8–10%, pistachios 11–12%) is traded, not manufactured, and sits below the
cashew-led blended EBITDA. Hitting the 70:30 mix target while holding the 16–20% EBITDA band requires the
utilisation-driven fixed-cost absorption to more than offset mix — that is the real thing to check in FY27.
Almonds are the volume trap. "the most voluminous product and the margins lies between 4% to 5%" —
revenue diversification into almonds inflates the topline and dilutes both margin and working-capital
efficiency simultaneously. Watch for FY27 revenue beating the manufacturing target while EBITDA doesn't.
The company just deleveraged into its own growth constraint. ₹9.5cr of IPO proceeds went to debt
repayment, yet the 85–90% utilisation target is gated on "additional working capital" — for a seasonal
Jan–May procurement business, the same rupee cannot both retire debt and fund the buying season.
CNSL is a margin story disguised as a capacity story. The shell is already generated and already
sold ("currently the cashew shell generated during processing is sold as a by-product"); the facility
converts an existing zero-effort by-product sale into an industrial oil plus a saleable biomass stream.
There is no incremental raw-material cost — which is why it could matter disproportionately to a company
with ₹9.24cr of EBITDA, and why the absence of any sizing on the call is the notable omission.
The freight escape was luck, not structure. FY26 avoided the container-cost spike purely because
dispatches began in May, after the spike. The exposure is unchanged for the next Jan–May procurement cycle.
Spices, not nuts, are the stated geographic unlock — a tell that management sees the nut portfolio as
structurally North/West-bound and is not pretending otherwise.
qoq change log (fill each quarter): H2 FY26 (this — FIRST note for NFPSAMPOOR, no prior baseline): FY26 revenue ₹51cr (+43%), EBITDA
₹9.24cr ("nearly doubled"), PAT ₹4.53cr (+68%). Full year in the 6,000 MT Ghiloth plant (moved June, FY26)
+ Yashvardhan Food Industries acquired. Processing 3,000–3,200 MT vs 1,800–1,900 MT in FY25. ~95% cashew,
94–95% B2B, 17 states, ~140 employees. IPO proceeds → ₹9.5cr debt repayment + working capital + GCP.
Guidance set: manufacturing ₹60–65cr FY27; volume 4,000–4,200 MT (65–70%); 85–90% utilisation in 2 years;
EBITDA band 16–20%; mix to 70:30; B2B to 90–93% with B2G the priority. CNSL commercial production guided
Aug–Sep 2026, machinery ordered. Mid-term margin guidance explicitly declined.
Next quarter → check: (1) did CNSL actually commercialise in Aug–Sep 2026, and what did it contribute
(the single hard-dated commitment on this call); (2) manufacturing revenue tracking to ₹60–65cr and
volume to 4,000–4,200 MT; (3) whether EBITDA margin held the 16–20% band as the lower-margin traded
portfolio scaled; (4) B2G share actually moving off ~2.5% — NAFED/GeM wins; (5) post-repayment debt and
D/E, the number management could not give; (6) whether working capital availability capped the utilisation
ramp; (7) freight/container cost impact on the Jan–May 2027 procurement window; (8) any H2-discrete
disclosure so the reporting is not full-year-only.

margins & cost dynamics: Company-level EBITDA: FY26 EBITDA ₹9.24cr, "nearly doubled". The transcript's FY26 margin % is garbled
(§2) and management never restated it. The only margin levels spoken on the call are the analyst's
premise ("the EBITDA margins are at a higher level which are before the IPO, which is 18%") and
management's own sustainable band, "16% to 20%".
Product-level margins (management, verbatim): raisins "10% to 12%"; almonds — "the most voluminous
product and the margins lies between 4% to 5%"; walnuts "8% to 10%"; pistachios "11% to 12%".
→ Diversifying away from cashew is margin-dilutive at the product line, which management conceded
directly: "in other products, the margin is slightly lesser because we are into trading part of that and
this is, there's no certain kind of manufacturing which can be done in other products."
B2C economics: "the gross margin is around 30% to 25% and the COGS around 70%."
The stated margin lever is fixed-cost absorption, not price: "we have been targeting to increase the
volume in processing, which will help us to have a better utilization of the capacity, which will reduce
the fixed cost of the plant and other indirect expenses, which can help us improve the EBITDA margins."
Labour: the Yashvardhan Food Industries acquisition "reduced our dependency on the labor cost".
Freight / logistics (see §10 and §13): volatility acknowledged but FY26 impact denied on timing grounds
— "because our raw material dispatches have started since May only, so we have not been affected that
much … the shipments have started now and the prices have come down again, so there's not a major impact
in the freight costs."
Named margin risks: "there are cross-border imports which are involved and, you know, there are some
uncertain situations such as increase in the local freight cost of containers or prices hike in
transportations."
capex / expansion (watch slippage): CNSL extraction facility — the only dated capex item. "We have already ordered the required machinery
and we are expecting the commercial production from August to September in 2026." Capex amount not
disclosed; expected revenue/margin not disclosed. Slippage watch: machinery-ordered → commercial
production inside ~2 months of the call is a tight window for a first-time process line.
Processing plant: already-executed capex — the FY26 move "in June from our earlier smaller unit" to the
6,000 MT facility. No new processing-capacity capex was announced; the plan is to fill the existing
6,000 MT ("we are targeting in next two years with additional working capital … to reach at least 85% to
90% of capacity utilization"), i.e. the next two years' growth is guided to be working-capital-funded,
not capex-funded.
Spices remain pre-capex: "we are in the R&D stage of that."
capital allocation: IPO proceeds, in management's words: "The object of the issue was used in part of it was used in the
debt repayment, part of it was used in the working capital which will be -- which is used in increasing
the capacity utilization and part of it was GCP and issue expenses."
Debt repayment quantum: "we are repaying around INR9.5 crores of debt towards from the issue proceeds."
Management could not confirm the resulting leverage on the call — "that I have to exactly check how much".
Stated rationale: "when we are repaying the debt, it will directly benefit our EBITDA levels, the PAT
margin levels in further and future and the working capital will benefit us in having a better reach
towards the capacity utilization and also penetrating into other verticals of dry fruit trading."
M&A: one acquisition executed in FY26 (Yashvardhan Food Industries Private Limited); consideration not
disclosed on the call.
No dividend, buyback or further fund-raise was discussed.
risks & watch-items: Single-product concentration: ~95% cashew today; the 70:30 target is medium-term and the diversifying
products carry lower margins (§7).
Single-channel concentration: B2B at "94%, 95%"; B2G is the stated fix but is tender-driven and
currently near-nil.
Commodity + import exposure, acknowledged by management as the reason the margin band can break:
"because it is a commodity business, there is slight fluctuation … there are cross-border imports which
are involved."
Freight/container cost: acknowledged as an industry-wide problem in the prior 2–3 months ("all
industries are facing some trans-logistic problems … Yes, it is there"), escaped in FY26 only by
procurement seasonality — "the procurement period for cashew nuts or any other products is generally from
January to May". A repeat of the freight spike inside the Jan–May FY28 procurement window would land
squarely on cost.
Working capital is the binding constraint on the utilisation ramp — the 85–90% target is explicitly
conditioned on "additional working capital", against a business that has just used IPO money to deleverage.
Leverage: analyst-cited D/E of 1.73 for FY26 against ₹9.5cr of repayment; management did not confirm
the post-repayment number.
CNSL execution risk: first-time process, no capex/return disclosed, tight Aug–Sep 2026 window.
Disclosure quality: no H2-discrete P&L, no consolidated FY27 revenue guidance, no capex quantum, and a
garbled EBITDA-margin statement that went uncorrected on the call.
Governance/liquidity structure: NSE SME (Series SM), micro-cap, first year of listed disclosure.
management quality / tone: Measured and unusually concrete for an SME first-year call: the MD volunteered volumes (MT), per-product
margin bands and channel percentages without being pushed, and answered the awkward "is 18% sustainable in a
commodity business?" question head-on with a band and its failure conditions rather than a deflection. Two
tone markers worth carrying forward. First, he declined to give a mid-term margin aspiration on
compliance grounds — "I'm not allowed to specify anything regarding the numbers of future-looking statements"
— restraint, though it sat oddly beside the FY27 manufacturing, volume and mix targets he had already given.
Second, he could not answer the post-repayment leverage question ("that I have to exactly check how
much") and allowed the analyst to supply the debt figures; the CFO (Mr. Anil Kumar Gupta) was on the call but
did not speak at any point in the transcript. Diversification was framed honestly as margin-dilutive rather
than sold as accretive. Only five questions were asked, by two analysts, and the call ran ~8 transcript
pages — coverage is thin and the disclosures are unaudited-by-questioning.
non-obvious takeaways: The 43% growth is a plant-move artefact more than a demand event. Management said so plainly: "the
growth is purely because of the better utilization of the capacity during the last fiscal year." FY25 ran
1,800–1,900 MT in a smaller unit; FY26 ran 3,000–3,200 MT in the new one. The comparable FY27 delta
(3,200 → 4,000–4,200 MT) is ~25–31% on volume, a materially slower step — the 43% is not the run-rate.
Diversification and margin pull in opposite directions. Every product being added (almonds 4–5%,
raisins 10–12%, walnuts 8–10%, pistachios 11–12%) is traded, not manufactured, and sits below the
cashew-led blended EBITDA. Hitting the 70:30 mix target while holding the 16–20% EBITDA band requires the
utilisation-driven fixed-cost absorption to more than offset mix — that is the real thing to check in FY27.
Almonds are the volume trap. "the most voluminous product and the margins lies between 4% to 5%" —
revenue diversification into almonds inflates the topline and dilutes both margin and working-capital
efficiency simultaneously. Watch for FY27 revenue beating the manufacturing target while EBITDA doesn't.
The company just deleveraged into its own growth constraint. ₹9.5cr of IPO proceeds went to debt
repayment, yet the 85–90% utilisation target is gated on "additional working capital" — for a seasonal
Jan–May procurement business, the same rupee cannot both retire debt and fund the buying season.
CNSL is a margin story disguised as a capacity story. The shell is already generated and already
sold ("currently the cashew shell generated during processing is sold as a by-product"); the facility
converts an existing zero-effort by-product sale into an industrial oil plus a saleable biomass stream.
There is no incremental raw-material cost — which is why it could matter disproportionately to a company
with ₹9.24cr of EBITDA, and why the absence of any sizing on the call is the notable omission.
The freight escape was luck, not structure. FY26 avoided the container-cost spike purely because
dispatches began in May, after the spike. The exposure is unchanged for the next Jan–May procurement cycle.
Spices, not nuts, are the stated geographic unlock — a tell that management sees the nut portfolio as
structurally North/West-bound and is not pretending otherwise.
